[LSER.9.3.2] The eviction sweep runs once per pump (engine cycle),
reading the engine clock once — the same `now_ns` and cadence as the
TTL fact sweep ([LFAC.1.3.3], [LFST.6.1]), **not** a real OS timer.
The engine clock is a recorded input in replay ([LDET.1.8.2]) and
every event-trace event carries its clock, so the sweep reads the
same `now_ns` at the same logical points on replay; eviction — and
the cold-start re-warm it triggers — is reproduced identically, as
part of the replay contract in [LDET.2.2a]. Evicted state means the
allocation is freed and the next sample for that identity cold-starts
a fresh allocation. The value `nulls: hold` repeats is not evicted
([LNUL.8.6]). Because eviction advances only when a pump reads
an advanced clock, a backing in a fully silent window is not freed
until the next assertion or `$ClockTick` ([LFST.6.2]) — the same
trigger dependency the signal aggregations carry ([LSIG.7]).
